item.title: Kanye West’s controversial concerts in Russia have finally been cancelled
item.description: According to the Moscow-based organizer Say Agency, the controversial rapper's two October dates in St Petersburg have been cancelled. Russian media states that the decision was made by the authorities, who are reportedly investigating the organizers for alleged fraud.

item.title: Can Canada be the EU's answer to 'unreliable' trade partners?
item.description: Ahead of October's EU-Canada summit, both sides are considering a partnership beyond CETA and €130 billion in annual trade. Nothing is agreed on financial services, and the new "associate member" tier has no legal definition.

item.title: Rutte responds to Moscow's nuclear threats, and the UK leader weighs re-joining the EU
item.description: Good morning, I’m Mared Gwyn. Welcome to your Thursday newsletter. Today: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte tells Euronews that Russia should stop issuing nuclear threats, and the UK Prime Minister puts EU membership back on the table.

item.title: Before the Iran war vs now: How much of a worker’s wage is needed to fill a 50-litre tank?
item.description: A 50-litre diesel tank costs the equivalent of 15.4% of Bulgaria’s gross monthly minimum wage, compared with 3.8% in Luxembourg, as fuel prices have risen since the Iran war began.

item.title: Europe Today: Rutte tells Russia to stop nuclear threats at Euronews defence summit
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte tells Russia to stop its nuclear threats, speaking at the Euronews Defence Summit as Moscow threatens to use its nuclear arsenal. Rutte also said there's no imminent threat to NATO territory, while Belgian defence chief Theo Francken argued Russia is Belgium's biggest threat.

item.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike in hospital after surviving two lethal injections, lawyers say
item.description: Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed Colleen Slemmer, 19, at a job training camp for young people.

item.title: 'Women don't cry any more, they cash in': Shakira turns Madrid into a festival of empowerment
item.description: The Colombian pop star returns to Spain after eight years with a 12-show residency in Madrid, celebrating Latin culture and turning a chapter of her life into a spectacle of music, freedom and empowerment.

item.title: Hundreds held, dozens wounded as protests over conditions in French schools escalate
item.description: Since last week, students have staged protests outside schools over grievances ranging from timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers to overheated classrooms during this year's heatwaves.

item.title: Where does body fat go when we lose weight? The answer is stranger than you expect
item.description: Researchers estimate that around 84% of lost body fat is exhaled as carbon dioxide, while the remaining 16% is lost as water.

item.title: Methane is responsible for 30% of global warming – so why is the EU trying to delay rules to cut it?
item.description: “Methane is the quickest brake we have on warming this decade. Before ministers agree to ease off it, I'd ask them to look very carefully at what it actually costs.”

item.title: Explained: How the EU’s new cabin baggage rules will work – and when they start
item.description: EU travellers could soon get a larger cabin allowance at no extra cost – but UK passengers flying out of UK airports are unlikely to benefit from the new rules.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 1st, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 1st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Japan's Sanae Takaichi announces new tightened measures for foreigners seeking permanent residency
item.description: The measures come as the country’s conservative leader Sanae Takaichi looks to deliver on election promises, which were spearheaded by vast immigration reforms, in her historic supermajority election victory in February.

item.title: “I grabbed the controls”: FlyDubai survivor recounts dramatic cockpit attack as he meets Netanyahu
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Yaniv Hayun, one of the passengers who helped subdue a pilot after a stabbing on a Flydubai flight bound for Israel.

item.title: US-led coalition ends anti-Islamic State mission in Iraq amid heightened regional tensions and security fears
item.description: The US-led force has been operating in Iraq for 12 years to dismantle ISIS networks which had threatened to takeover the region and plunge it into instability.

item.title: 'Alternative Nobel' honours women taking on authoritarian rule, patriarchy and Big Tech
item.description: Four winners from 200 nominees are honoured for standing up to authoritarian rule, patriarchal violence and unchecked AI development.

item.title: Ronaldo quits Portugal camp ahead of Denmark clash, promising to reveal 'the truth'
item.description: The 41-year-old captain announced his departure on Instagram minutes after coach Jorge Jesus insisted he would train, having missed three sessions in a row.

item.title: Burnham says 'strong indications' Iran played part in UK airbase security scare
item.description: Tehran has rejected any involvement in Sunday's incident at the US-used airbase, where police found petrol but no explosives and five suspects have been released on bail.

item.title: Can cities cope with Europe's tourism boom? MEPs debate in a special edition of The Ring
item.description: In this special live episode, we’re zooming in on how the tourism boom across Europe is affecting locals — and whether it’s possible to square the circle between the continent’s tourism growth and its worrying housing crisis.

item.title: TAP: final bids from Air France-KLM and Lufthansa have been submitted
item.description: Air France-KLM and Lufthansa submitted their final bids on Wednesday to buy a 44.9% stake in TAP, closing the bidding phase and leaving the decision to the government.

item.title: AIIB reaffirms commitment to close global infrastructure financing gap at Doha meeting
item.description: The 11th AIIB annual meeting brings policymakers, investors and business leaders from around the world to Doha to explore how technology, sustainability, connectivity and investment are reshaping the way cities and economies develop.

item.title: UK ends 'one in, one out' migrant returns deal with France
item.description: Only about 4% of small-boat arrivals were sent back under the year-long pilot, which cost an average of €65,500 per return, as Paris pushes for an EU-wide replacement.

item.title: From nuclear to hybrid: The key moments from the Euronews Defence Summit
item.description: Euronews hosted on Wednesday its first Defence and Space Summit. Here are the key moments from the day-long gathering, bringing together the NATO Secretary General, ministers, senior officials and industry leaders.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | September 30th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: The War in the Sky: Kyiv braces for another winter of Russian attacks
item.description: A Euronews documentary goes inside Ukraine’s battle to defend its skies, from air-defence crews battling Russia’s drone threats to workers repairing the damage and families preparing for another winter of attacks.

item.title: Bardella hits back at Macron over antisemitism allegations
item.description: The far-right National Rally party's Jordan Bardella has denied being the author of antisemitic messages attributed to him by investigative outlet Mediapart, which were published on Monday.

item.title: European preference in defence is a 'luxury' debate, NATO chief tells Euronews
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte told Euronews the European preference debate is a "luxury" since neither Europe nor the US can meet the growing demand for defence products and the industry should ramp up its capacity.

item.title: Macron backs Spain over Ceuta migration crisis and urges firm EU action
item.description: Sánchez and Macron back cooperation between Spain and France and call for greater EU unity on migration, economic and geopolitical issues, despite the Spanish Senate's rejection of the bilateral Friendship Treaty.

item.title: Qatar and UAE back Ethiopian government as fighting spreads beyond Tigray
item.description: Fighting has displaced an estimated 150,000 people, drawing responses from Qatar and the UAE as Ethiopia and its neighbours trade accusations.

item.title: Uzeyir Hajibeyli festival celebrates a lasting musical legacy
item.description: Uzeyir Hajibeyli’s musical legacy continues to bring different traditions together, inspiring an international festival spanning concerts, culture and musical exchange.

item.title: ‘There is no immediate threat to NATO territory,’ Secretary General Rutte tells Euronews
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte told Euronews there is no immediate threat to the alliance and he does not take Russia's Kaliningrad nuclear warning seriously, saying Moscow is trying to distract from its struggles in Ukraine.

item.title: BMW's strategy: Job cuts, AI and a €2bn bet on ‘Made in Germany’
item.description: German premium carmaker BMW Group is investing around €2 billion in vehicle production and battery manufacturing in Germany, as it unveils plans to rebuild profitability.

item.title: ‘Let workers have a say’: Protesters target OpenAI conference
item.description: Dozens of activists protested outside OpenAI's developer conference in San Francisco, calling on the company to end its contracts with the US military and Immigration and Customs Enforcement and demanding greater regulation of AI.

item.title: Spain to investigate claims its soldiers have tortured migrants in Ceuta
item.description: Amnesty International says it has documented beatings, humiliations, summary expulsions and racial profiling in Ceuta and the Spanish government has ordered the military to identify any individuals potentially responsible.

item.title: These 10 airlines have the best in-flight wifi – and only one is European
item.description: If you’re looking to get online while in the air, you might just want to book a flight with Qatar Airways, Delta or United.

item.title: EU-backed scheme helps rural Swedish households on lower incomes go electric
item.description: A Swedish government scheme, part-funded by the EU's Social Climate Fund, is offering rural, lower-income drivers financial support to switch from petrol and diesel to electric vehicles.

item.title: Grand Voyager | Exploring Berlin beyond the landmarks
item.description: Berlin is a city filled with history, creativity and energy, from street art on the Berlin Wall to cycling through its leafy streets. In this episode, Lilly Douse discovers what brings Germany’s capital to life.

item.title: Kubilius: Europe's response to Russian hybrid attacks should be 'as painful' for Moscow
item.description: The European Commissioner for Defence tells Euronews that the EU must sharpen its response to a growing spate of hybrid attacks attributed to Moscow, while rejecting those who say it's time to engage the Kremlin in diplomacy.

item.title: Bulgaria's parliament passes law protecting journalists from abusive SLAPP lawsuits
item.description: Most SLAPPs are for defamation or reputational harm and tend to be used by those rich and powerful enough to afford the necessary lawyers' fees.

item.title: US presses Europe to release more emergency oil reserves as prices surge
item.description: Washington says European countries have yet to deliver promised oil releases, as soaring crude and diesel prices intensify pressure on governments to intervene.

item.title: Inflation accelerates again in Italy: September rate hits 4.2%, a three-year high
item.description: Consumer price index accelerates driven by energy goods and fresh food. Between historical memory and daily worries, Istat records a sharp drop in confidence among households and firms.

item.title: No more radio silence: EU plans cross-border lifeline for emergency services
item.description: When disaster strikes near a border, police and firefighters can lose contact the moment they cross it. Brussels wants a 5G network, backed by satellites, to change that by 2036.

item.title: Bulgarian PM Rumen Radev urges European dialogue with Russia to avert nuclear attack
item.description: "We always need to think about the worst-case scenario," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said at the Euronews' Defence Summit, warning of the risk of a Russian nuclear attack if tensions with Europe escalate.

item.title: EU commercial flights rise despite higher jet fuel prices
item.description: The number of commercial flights across the EU increased in every summer month compared with last year, although traffic fell in several member states.

item.title: Europe’s defence industry ‘not ready’ for rearmament push, Estonian MEP warns
item.description: Estonian MEP and former general Riho Terras backed buying weapons from outside the EU during debate on defence spending.

item.title: Exclusive: Ukraine's partners could access new tech to counter jet-powered drones, Budanov tells Euronews
item.description: Countries with existing drone cooperation agreements with Kyiv could negotiate access to Ukraine’s latest technology for countering Russia’s new jet-powered drones, Kyrylo Budanov told Euronews.

item.title: Thousands of firefighters march in Paris demanding more resources
item.description: Nearly 8,000 French firefighters marched through Paris, calling for more staff and funding and protesting what unions describe as a lack of government action.

item.title: UK growth revised up to 0.5%: What drove the stronger figures?
item.description: Stronger services growth drove the upward revision to second-quarter GDP growth, as the UK battles high borrowing costs, inflationary pressures and a cooling labour market.

item.title: UK's Burnham floats going ‘all the way’ and rejoining the EU
item.description: The British Prime Minister has said he will weigh a “range of options” for the future relationship with the European Union, including the prospect of rejoining the bloc.

item.title: Norwegian ministers grilled in parliament over ties to convicted sex offender Epstein
item.description: Parliament has also set up an independent inquiry tasked with a much broader examination of the case, which is due to submit its final report by 31 January 2028.
